text.p: Construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it believed Australia was starting to see the beginning of an upswing in construction activity which would peak in the year 2000.
"(Construction) volumes are moving up to the highest levels, in real dollar terms, that they have ever been," Leighton's managing director, Wal King told a news conference.
King said Leighton expected construction activity to peak at about five percent of Australia's gross domestic product by about the year 2000.
Leighton earlier announced a 17 percent rise in half year net earnings to A$34.5 million and forecast continued steady earnings growth for the year to June 30.
"For the next period ahead we expect growth in Australia and Asia - all graphs are up," King said.
Leighton's current low level of debt and high level of undrawn facilities put it in an excellent position to make acquisitions, King said.
"The company wishes to continue to grow, if there were any suitable opportunities around we would have a look at them but nothing has been brought to us of interest," he said.
King said Leighton was looking for growth from infrastructure projects and was prepared to use its balance sheet to facilitate developments but was cautious about diversifying its activities.
"We are not opposed to diversification but it would have to fit very closely within our guidelines," he said.
King said the company saw tremendous opportunities in the area of telecommunications in Asia, particularly in Indonesia.
In September last year the company's Theiss unit won a joint venture contract worth A$200 million for supply, installation and commissioning of telecommunications cable in Central Java.
Late last year Leighton acquired the broadband rollout unit, Visionstream, of telecommunications carrier, Telstra Australia for an undisclosed amount.
At 1.450 p.m. (0345 GMT), Leighton shares were five cents weaker at A$5.80.
Leighton's largest shareholder is Hochtief Ag.
